observations.body: Outer decay and unseen glory alter affliction. Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day. while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.

payload.posture: Read 2 Corinthians 4:16–18 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states outer decay and unseen glory alter affliction. Therefore we don’t faint, but though our outward person is decaying, yet our inward person is renewed day by day. while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
